info.title: Binary counting
info.text: The input columns of a truth table are just binary numbers counting up: 000, 001, 010 and so on. That's why there are 2ⁿ rows.

info.title: De Morgan's law
info.text: NOT (A AND B) always gives the same result as NOT A OR NOT B. This rule, called De Morgan's law, lets engineers simplify circuits.

info.title: Light switches
info.text: The two-way light switches at the top and bottom of many staircases work like an XOR gate: flipping either switch changes the light.

info.title: Truth tables everywhere
info.text: Engineers use truth tables to test that circuits do exactly what they should, before building them.

info.title: Short circuits
info.text: In real circuits, each extra gate adds a tiny delay. Designers try to use as few gates as possible.

info.title: Big tables
info.text: A circuit with 10 inputs would need a truth table with 1,024 rows, so computers check large circuits automatically.
